clusters.name: Auth bootstrap error-surface mismatch
affected_flows: 02 Auth bootstrap — 05 backend unreachable > shows API_UNREACHABLE error with retry button
02 Auth bootstrap — 05 backend unreachable > retry button re-triggers bootstrap
02 Auth bootstrap — 07 forbidden > shows error state on 403 from /auth/me
02 Auth bootstrap — 07 forbidden > 403 error does not show retry button
clusters.hypothesis: Playwright expects protected-route error rendering, but the real browser snapshot lands on LoginPage. The dominant local hypothesis is a bootstrap/session transition mismatch between AuthContext, ProtectedRoute and the real API/auth fixtures, not a missing ErrorState component itself.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Re-run only scenario 05/07 with request logging for /auth/me and current localStorage after the transition to determine whether token/auth state is cleared before ProtectedRoute renders bootstrapError.

02 Auth bootstrap — 08 logout > after logout, localStorage is cleared
05 Upload flow > shows error when submitting without a file
05 Upload flow > uploads a text file and completes the import job

06 Search flow > search returns results or empty state without error
06 Search flow > search with workspace context sends request to real backend

09 Diagnostics GUI > diagnostics page accessible via admin nav link

clusters.hypothesis: Many failures share the Playwright symptom 'element is not stable' or 'element was detached'. This points to a remounting shell, route or auth-context transition that replaces the DOM while Playwright interacts, rather than isolated upload/search/chat defects.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Re-run one logout flow and one search flow with trace/video and inspect whether AppShell or the route subtree remounts between click target resolution and action commit.

clusters.name: Page contract drift in headings and labels
affected_flows: 05 Upload flow > shows upload form elements
07 Chat flow > shows chat page heading and workspace context
07 Chat flow > shows chat composer form

clusters.hypothesis: A subset of failures look like direct UI-text drift between the real pages and the truth specs: missing expected headings/cards or renamed surface labels. These are likely test-contract mismatches layered on top of the broader remount issue.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Compare rendered headings/labels from a clean authed browser snapshot against each failing expectation before changing feature code.

frontend.root_cause_summary: The frontend failures do not form 22 independent defects. The primary pattern is a bootstrap/shell transition problem that either clears or replaces the protected-route surface unexpectedly, with a smaller secondary cluster of UI-label drift in chat/diagnostics/upload truth specs.

clusters.name: Entropy helper or metric-model breakage
clusters.hypothesis: The concentration inside test_entropy_truth.py suggests a common issue in entropy helpers, metric collection or assumptions about current schema/test fixtures, rather than seven independent feature regressions.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Run only test_entropy_truth.py with -x and inspect the first failure stack to decide whether the dominant break is metric collection, helper seeding, or repair helper semantics.

clusters.name: Queue drift and dead-letter recovery instability
clusters.hypothesis: These failures cluster around queue status aging, retryable jobs, dead-letter accounting and stale import retry recovery. That points to one stability slice in background job lifecycle or queue metric accounting.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Run the single stale import retry test plus the queue backlog entropy tests to compare whether the bug is in job state transitions or only in metrics/repair accounting.

clusters.name: Retrieval and stale-index repair divergence
clusters.hypothesis: These failures form a single slice around lifecycle status, is_searchable, retrieval coverage and repair semantics. The benchmark can still be green while the lower-level entropy repair path is wrong or partially disconnected.
clusters.cheap_discriminating_check: Run only stale-index and retrieval entropy tests and compare DB-level is_searchable transitions before and after repair helpers.

backend.root_cause_summary: The backend red state is dominated by the entropy/stability slice, not by the core M4a/M4b/M4c truth slice. The strongest current hypothesis is a break in entropy helper assumptions or lower-level repair/metric accounting around drift, queue debt and stale-index/retrieval recovery.

recommended_fix_order: Frontend: isolate the auth-bootstrap error-surface mismatch for scenario 05/07 before touching upload/search/chat pages.
Frontend: inspect AppShell/auth remount behavior causing detached-element failures in logout/search/nav flows.
Backend: run test_entropy_truth.py with -x to capture the first failing primitive in entropy_helpers or repair semantics.
Backend: then resolve queue drift and stale-index/retrieval recovery as two separate stability slices.
